From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>

Marissa / team — notes below. I included a short example policy and auth options. Happy to expand during the call.

Auth / KMS: 
- We support API key rotation via Vault/KMS with short-lived keys. Recommended pattern: Redwood issues tenant-scoped API keys; customer uses Vault to store and rotate those keys; use mutual TLS or a VPC endpoint if you require private network.
- If Acme wants in-house control, we can support an auth proxy that mints short-lived Redwood tokens using the private KMS. Tradeoff: more infra on Acme side but tight key control.

Routing policy (pseudocode snippet)
-- start example --
policy {
  route: if (request.type == "chat" && latency_estimate < 120ms) -> region: us-east, model: rw-large-v2
  else if (request.type == "chat") -> try region: us-east, fallback model: rw-medium-v1
  else if (request.type == "batch_embedding") -> region: us-east, model: rw-embed-small, budget: cost_per_1000_tokens < $0.50
  retry_chain: [rw-large-v2 -> rw-medium-v1 -> rw-small-quant]
  geo_fallback: primary_region: us-east, failover_region: eu-west
}
-- end example --

Structured output: function-calling + schema validation is the recommended flow. Implementation: enable model function calling for the ticket.create tool with an explicit JSON schema; run a lightweight verifier model or deterministic validator on the output; if validation fails, run a constrained re-gen with stricter decoding params (temperature 0, top_p 0.0).

Embeddings/rerank: product suggestion: compute canonical embeddings at index time (rw-embed-large) and then at query time compute query embedding and rerank top-N using a lightweight cross-encoder or our reranker model to improve precision. For cost savings, use a two-stage pipeline: sparse retrieval -> embed-cosine top-200 -> rerank top-10.

Attachments: sample policy + recommended config in the call. I’ll bring a concrete routing JSON to the session.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai
